CUPS · WATER

Queen of Cups — Meaning

Cups

  • CategoryCups
  • SymbolWater / Cups (feelings, relationships) / Court card: Queen (empathy, intuition)
  • UprightBeing there, Kindness, Listening to feelings
  • ReversedToo considerate, Putting yourself last, A tired heart

A card about listening to another's feelings while treasuring your own.

Queen of Cups stands for "Being there, Kindness, Listening to feelings" when upright, and "Too considerate, Putting yourself last, A tired heart" when reversed. Rather than answering right away, try listening to the other person. Trying to understand their feelings can itself lead to peace of mind.

Reading it in a decision — In a situation where the other person's feelings sway, like caregiving, read this card as first taking the time to listen and try to understand their feelings, rather than producing an answer right away. Reversed, protect your own time to rest, so you do not carry too much in trying to fix the other person's mood.

The decision this speaks to: When you're torn about caregiving

SYMBOLS

The symbols in the picture

By the sea, the queen gazes at a lidded cup. What is inside cannot be seen from outside — a reminder that a person's heart cannot be fully known just by looking.

UPRIGHT

Upright meaning

  • Being there
  • Kindness
  • Listening to feelings

Rather than answering right away, try listening to the other person. Trying to understand their feelings can itself lead to peace of mind.

REVERSED

Reversed meaning

  • Too considerate
  • Putting yourself last

Do you feel you must somehow fix the other person's mood yourself? While treasuring them, it is fine to take time to rest yourself, too.

What you may not be noticing

FOR YOUR DECISION

Hints for your decision

How to read it when you are deciding

The Queen of Cups sits on a throne by the sea, gazing at a lidded cup. She is a person who deeply draws out others' feelings while also listening carefully to her own inner voice. In a decision, the power to stay close to the emotions around you is a strength — but check that prioritizing others' feelings has not made you lose sight of your own true heart. In a quiet place, with no one's expectations in the picture, ask 'what do I truly want?' and the answer surfaces.

How to face a familiar worry

This card often appears when you stand in a position of supporting someone and postpone your own choices. Reversed, watch that you are not being swept into the other person's emotions until the boundary blurs. Distinguishing between caring and carrying lets you decide while keeping your kindness.

Questions to ask yourself before you decide

With no one's expectations in the picture, what do you truly want? Prioritizing others' feelings, are you postponing your own true heart? Can you distinguish between caring and carrying? Do you have a place to think quietly?

"Ease of moving forward" is the strength of the tailwind behind an option if you move on it now — not a judgment of whether things will turn out well or badly.

Now that you have read the meaning, turn to the decision in front of you. Draw a card and lay your two options side by side.
